title: Project Critical Path Duration Analysis
real_world_story: A project manager is coordinating a complex product launch with multiple interdependent tasks. Some tasks cannot start until others are complete. Each task has a specific duration. The total time required to complete the project is determined by the 'Critical Path'—the longest sequence of dependent tasks. Any delay in a critical path task directly delays the entire project launch. To optimize the schedule, the manager needs to calculate the total duration of this critical path.
problem_statement: Given a set of N tasks with their respective durations and a set of M directed edges representing dependencies (edge u -> v means task u must be completed before task v can start), compute the maximum total duration of any path from any start node (node with no incoming edges) to any end node (node with no outgoing edges).
task: Implement an algorithm to find the longest path in a DAG. Use topological sorting to process nodes in order and Dynamic Programming to compute the maximum path duration to each node.
input_format: The first line contains two integers: N (number of tasks) and M (number of dependencies). The next N lines each contain an integer representing the duration of task i (for i = 0 to N-1). The next M lines each contain two integers u and v, indicating task u must precede task v.
expected_algorithm: Topological Sort followed by Dynamic Programming (Longest Path in DAG)
real_world_takeaway: Critical Path Method (CPM) is a foundational technique in project management. By identifying the longest chain of dependencies, managers can determine the minimum project duration and identify which tasks are 'critical' (have zero slack), allowing for better resource allocation.
